candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record provides strong evidence for Vibrio vulnificus as the causative organism: seawater/seafood exposure (shrimp cleaning), comma-shaped flagellate bacteria on microscopy, grass-green β-hemolytic colonies on blood agar, diabetic/alcoholic host with necrotizing soft tissue infection and sepsis, and procalcitonin >100 ng/mL with positive blood culture. C001 correctly identifies Gram-negative bacillus sepsis but remains at the parent/genus level without specifying Vibrio vulnificus, which is the required etiologic specificity of the benchmark diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Identifies sepsis with Gram-negative bacilli but omits the specific organism (Vibrio vulnificus) required by the benchmark reference

case_quality_flags: Microbiological findings (comma-shaped flagellate bacteria, β-hemolytic grass-green colonies on blood agar, seafood wound exposure in immunocompromised host) are highly characteristic of Vibrio vulnificus and strongly support the reference diagnosis
